- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent sentiment swings; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values if sentiment volatility >0.3.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict late-period prices (last 7–10 days); reduce forecast by 1–2% for days 25–30 if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model often misses the rebound; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for days 10–15 after sentiment turns positive.
